anchor.title: The infant Hercules and the Standard Oil serpents / Frank A. Nankivell 1906.
anchor.creator: Nankivell, Frank A. (Frank Arthur), 1869-1959, artist
anchor.citation: Nankivell, Frank A. \"The infant Hercules and the Standard Oil serpents.\" Political cartoon. New York: J. Ottmann Lith. Co., 1906. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Illus. in AP101.P7 1906 (Case X) [P&P], https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2011645893/.
anchor.rights: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
anchor.alt: A muscular baby Theodore Roosevelt, wearing a diaper and red cape, sits in a cradle strangling two large multi-headed serpents with human heads including John D. Rockefeller and Nelson W. Aldrich representing Standard Oil interests; the scene evokes the myth of infant Hercules slaying snakes, emphasizing Roosevelt's strength against trusts.
anchor.caption: This 1906 political cartoon depicts President Theodore Roosevelt as the infant Hercules strangling serpents representing Standard Oil and Senator Aldrich, symbolizing his aggressive trust-busting efforts to break up monopolies during the Progressive Era.

anchor.title: Woman suffrage parade, Wash., D.C.
anchor.creator: Buck, G. V. (George V.), photographer
anchor.citation: Buck, G. V. (George V.), photographer. Woman suffrage parade, Wash., D.C. 1913. Photograph. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, SSF - Women -- Politics and Suffrage -- 1913 [item] [P&P], LC-USZ62-34031 (b&w film copy neg.). https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2013648100/.
anchor.rights: Public Domain — No Known Restrictions on Publication
anchor.alt: A dense throng of suffragists in light-colored dresses and sashes marches down a wide urban avenue toward the U.S. Capitol dome visible in the distance, with an enormous unruly crowd pressing in from the sidewalks past the old Post Office building under overcast skies.
anchor.caption: Thousands of suffragists fill Pennsylvania Avenue during the 1913 Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington, D.C., marching for voting rights just before President Wilson's inauguration and highlighting women's demand for political equality.

anchor.alt: A vibrant chromolithograph political cartoon features a distressed woman labeled "Cuba" clutching the Cuban flag, ensnared in a large frying pan marked "Spanish Misrule" hovering over raging flames labeled "Anarchy." Below, on a green island, "Insurgents" clash with "Autonomists." The composition urges rescue from this dire predicament amid the Spanish-American War tensions. (62 words)
anchor.caption: This 1898 political cartoon depicts Cuba trapped between Spanish misrule and anarchy, urging U.S. intervention during the Spanish-American War, which relates to Tennessee standard US.26 on U.S. emergence as a world power.
